variants.name: Live signal: JCI, rupiah, INDOGB 10Y trend, INDOGB–UST spread
US 10Y trend in place of the INDOGB trend
Korea-style rotation (JCI inverted: stocks down = bonds up)

ust.method: Overnight = New York closes strictly before each Jakarta close (New York shuts at about 04:00–05:00 Jakarta). Hedged = INDOGB 10Y minus β × US 10Y, β the trailing 26-week weekly beta known at the time. All variants walk-forward, z-scores vs trailing 52 weeks, thresholds ±0.5, hit rates over the next 4 weeks. The 'Beta 3Y' slot carries the INDOGB 15Y.

src: Yahoo Finance: IDX Composite (^JKSE) and USD/IDR (IDR=X) daily closes; any USD/IDR close more than 1.5% from Bank Indonesia’s JISDOR fix is replaced by JISDOR. INDOGB 10Y: PHEI IGSYC (CNBC benchmark 10Y before the first stored PHEI day). US Treasury daily par yields (2Y, 10Y; home.treasury.gov). Weekly, last trading day of each week.

method.window: 4-week changes; z-scores vs trailing 52 weeks (min 26); thresholds ±0.5
components: USD/IDR 4-week % change (inverted: a weaker rupiah is bond-bearish)
INDOGB − UST 10Y spread vs its 26-week average (wide = cheap)

method.window: 20-day changes; z-scores vs trailing 260 sessions (min 130); spread vs its 130-day average; thresholds ±0.5; hit rates over the next 20 sessions; UST hedge β = trailing 130-day daily beta
components: INDOGB − UST 10Y spread vs its 130-day average (wide = cheap)

notes.headline: A day after BI's hike JISDOR sets a record 18,269, the JCI falls a fourth day (−1.02%) and the 10Y INDOGB edges to a new high of 7.74% even as Treasuries rally 3bp. The signal eases to −0.73 and the sell-off episode since Sep 28 is +53.1bp. Signal −0.73: bond sell-off
notes.now: The JCI fell 1.02% to 5,194.14, its fourth straight loss, with foreigners net sellers of Rp563.6bn across the market, while JISDOR fixed 0.09% weaker at a record 18,269 and spot 0.12% weaker at 18,254 as most Asian currencies firmed, so BI's hike has not yet steadied the rupiah. Over 20 sessions the JCI is down 12.5% and USD/IDR up 1.83%; BI puts the year-to-date foreign equity outflow at Rp81.6tn against Rp143tn of inflows into SBN and SRBI, which does not rule out bond selling since, and who traded bonds today is not published. The daily signal is −0.73 (−0.88 yesterday on today's rebuild): the 10Y trend part is the most bearish (z +1.77, the 10Y up 52.8bp over 20 sessions), then the JCI part (z −1.21) and the rupiah part (z +0.65), while the spread part (z +0.70) leans bond-bullish. INDOGBs pay 266.9bp over Treasuries, 20.0bp above the 130-day average and in the 85th percentile of 52 weeks, up from 262.9bp because the US 10Y fell about 3bp to 5.07% while the INDOGB 10Y rose; that is a nominal pick-up before currency risk. At the 1-year daily beta of 0.28 the US move implied −0.8bp for the INDOGB 10Y, which rose 1.0bp, so Treasuries explain none of today's move; the 60-day beta is only 0.14 and the next-day spill-over beta 0.069. Over four weeks the INDOGB 10Y is up 28.1bp and the US 10Y 11bp, but with a 26-week weekly beta of −0.13 the Treasury-linked part is −1.4bp and +29.5bp is residual, the part the US move does not explain, not proof of domestic selling or political risk. On the daily build the sell-off episode that began Sep 28 is still open, 29 sessions and +53.1bp. Since July 2022 the daily signal scores a Sharpe of 0.80 outright and 0.86 hedged against Treasuries, but sell-off calls were right only 52.3% of the time over the next 20 sessions (rally calls 57.9%, hedged 64.8%) and the 10Y rose just 0.1bp on average after a sell-off call; these are in-sample back-tests. Our read for the next 2–4 weeks: neutral on duration rather than short, because sell-off calls have had no edge; the rupiah's response to the hike, the Q3 balance of payments on Nov 20 and the Dec 9 Fed decision are the main risks, mostly to the 1–5Y.
notes.flip: The daily signal is in sell-off below −0.5 and sits at −0.73. A return to neutral needs the 10Y trend to cool as the late-October jump rolls out of the 20-session window, plus a JCI back above 5,300 with the rupiah near 18,050. A deeper sell-off would come from JISDOR moving further past today's 18,269 record, a JCI relapse below 4,900 or the 10Y extending above today's 7.74% high. A move to bond rally (above +0.5) needs a JCI rebound with foreign buying and a firmer rupiah together, the pattern that started the April 2025 rally. The policy triggers: BI's Nov 18 hike has to steady the rupiah to help the trend part (our read; BI has not committed to a level), a December BI hike or a Fed hike on Dec 9 (50bp has been floated) would hit the front end and belly, and MSCI softening its Standalone proposal would help the equity part.
phases: JCI 6,500–7,250 while the 10Y rose from 6.2% to a 7.58% peak in October 2022 as global rates surged; stocks held up on the commodity boom.

JCI 6,630–7,380 and 10Y 6.19–7.21%. Stocks and bonds drifted without a clear link; on the weekly build the signal's calls lost money (Sharpe −0.3 from 2022 to August 2024), while the daily build did better over the same span.
JCI fell from 7,812 to 6,258 while the 10Y rose from 6.43% to 7.19%: stocks, rupiah and bonds sold off together, the pattern the signal is built for. Its record improves sharply from here.
JCI climbed from 6,262 to a record 9,075 on Jan 15, 2026, and the 10Y fell to 5.93% in October 2025 as foreign money returned and BI eased.

MSCI froze Indonesian index changes in January and on Oct 15 proposed Standalone status; BI hiked 100bp to 5.75% by June and another 25bp to 6.00% on Nov 18. JCI −42% from its peak to about 5,194, 10Y up to 7.74%: the second and deeper foreign exit, though foreigners bid Rp18tn at the Nov 10 auction and BI reports SBN/SRBI inflows for the year. Vice President Gibran resigned on Nov 12 and JISDOR set records on Nov 16, 17 and 19, the last a day after BI's hike; INDOGBs absorbed Treasury swings in both directions with little link, and the daily signal sat between −0.7 and −0.9.
notes.caveats: These are proxies, not reported fund flows: daily foreign SBN holdings (DJPPR) and equity flows (IDX) are not machine-readable for the dashboard, so the rupiah and the JCI stand in for foreign money, and any statement about who bought or sold is a hypothesis. USD/IDR is Yahoo's close, replaced by Bank Indonesia's JISDOR fix on any day it strays more than 1.5% (Yahoo printed ~17,480 from Nov 3, 2026 while JISDOR was ~18,100); the 20-session windows count stored sessions, so gaps in the data stretch them and added sessions restate past signals. Before Oct 29, 2026 the 10Y is CNBC's benchmark-bond yield rather than PHEI's IGSYC, with repeated stale prints removed. The daily back-test runs from July 2022 (961 sessions): the live signal makes 201.6bp outright (Sharpe 0.80) and 210.2bp hedged against Treasuries (Sharpe 0.86), against −45.0bp for always holding the 10Y; the weekly build scores 0.57 and 0.75. Variants that use the US 10Y trend score up to 0.92 outright and 0.95 hedged on the weekly build but were picked after the fact and are not live. In-sample, no trading costs; not a trading system.
